capitals.name: Mombasa (Fort Jesus)
capitals.note: Fort Jesus 'built between 1593 and 1596 by order of King Felipe II of Spain'; the Portuguese held Mombasa from 1589 (Mombasa page).

correction.text: Mombasa with Fort Jesus and the islands the siege page has falling to the Omanis in 1698: 'the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba' (the footprint is the researcher's reading of Mombasa, Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa Island)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1589-1729: the Portuguese footprint north of Cape Delgado. The Mombasa page has the Portuguese taking Mombasa 'a third time in 1589' and Fort Jesus (1593-1596); the siege page has Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa Island taken by the Omanis after Mombasa fell in 1698. No page gives the area, so the footprint is the town with the islands, not a drawn coastline; Malindi, Pate and Faza are not shown as Portuguese territory (the siege page does not say Faza was Portuguese). From 1698 to 1728 the land is Omani and the ledger takes it away.

ledger.note: 1589: the Portuguese take Mombasa a third time. 'This stimulated the Portuguese to take over Mombasa a third time in 1589' after the Ottoman admiral 'Ali Bey's capture of 1585 and the Zimba raids; they built Fort Jesus 'four years later' (1593; the Fort Jesus page: 'between 1593 and 1596') and placed Mombasa 'under members of the ruling family of Malindi'.

1631: Sultan Yusuf ibn al-Hasan takes Fort Jesus. 'the Portuguese lost it to Sultan Yusuf ibn al-Hasan of Mombasa'; the Mombasa page: 'In 1631 Dom Jeronimo, the ruler of Mombasa, slaughtered the Portuguese garrison in the city'.

1632: the Portuguese recapture Mombasa. 'After the Portuguese recaptured it from the Sultan in 1632'; the Mombasa page: 'That year the Portuguese returned and established direct rule over Mombasa'; Dom Jeronimo 'left and became a pirate'.
13 March 1696: the Omani siege of Fort Jesus begins. The siege lasted 'from 13 March 1696 to 13 December 1698'.
13 December 1698: Fort Jesus falls. 'The last Omani attack on December 13 captured the fort.'

region.text: Mombasa with Fort Jesus and the islands the siege page has falling to the Omanis in 1698: 'the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba' (the footprint is the researcher's reading of Mombasa, Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa Island)

ledger.note: 13 December 1698: the Omani capture of Mombasa. 'the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba fell to the Omani Arabs'; the Omanis drove 'out the last Portuguese settlers' from Zanzibar and began 'capturing Pemba Island, Kilwa Island' after the fall of Mombasa. The Mombasa page dates the capture 12 December 1698; the siege page's 13 December is used.

12 March 1728: the Portuguese return to Mombasa. The rulers list has the Portuguese Álvaro Caetano de Melo Castro in office '12 Mar 1728 - 21 Sep 1729'; the Fort Jesus page: they 'briefly captured and re-occupied it between 1728 and 1729'. Only the town is recorded as regained.
21 September 1729: Portuguese rule at Mombasa ends. The Portuguese captain's term ends '21 Sep 1729' and the infobox gives 'Sultanate of Oman 1729-1824'.

wars.name: Revolt of Yusuf ibn al-Hasan (Dom Jeronimo)
wars.outcome: The Sultan of Mombasa slaughtered the Portuguese garrison in 1631 and held Fort Jesus until the Portuguese recaptured it in 1632; he fled and became a pirate.

wars.name: Siege of Fort Jesus

zones.text: Mombasa with Fort Jesus and the islands the siege page has falling to the Omanis in 1698: 'the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba' (the footprint is the researcher's reading of Mombasa, Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa Island)

wars.outcome: Omani victory: the fort fell on 13 December 1698; Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa Island were then taken by the Omanis; relief fleets from Lisbon reached the island only after the fall.
wars.note: The page elsewhere says the siege 'was lifted in December 1696'; the span 13 March 1696 to 13 December 1698 is its own summary. Portuguese squadrons of 1699, 1700 and 1701 failed.

certainty.note: A fortified town and island dependencies: no boundary on the pages.

sources.title: Mombasa
sources.note: Mombasa history: Portuguese 1593-1698, 1631 revolt, 1698 Omani capture, Mazrui independence 1746, British protectorate 1824-1826, annexation by Said 24 June 1837, 1887 relinquished to the British East Africa Association, 1895.

sources.title: Fort Jesus
sources.note: Fort built 1593-1596; Sultan Yusuf ibn al-Hasan took it in 1631, Portuguese back 1632; Omani siege 1696-1698; Portuguese again 1728-1729; local rule 1741-1837; Omani capture 1837.

sources.title: Siege of Fort Jesus
sources.note: 13 March 1696 to 13 December 1698; Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa fall to the Omanis; Mombasa Omani until 1728.

notes:
New state (a colony of the Portuguese Empire; Cliopatria lacks the Portuguese coast). Three pages: Mombasa, Fort Jesus, Siege of Fort Jesus. There is no Wikipedia article called 'Portuguese Mombasa' (the title was tried and did not load).

Dates that disagree: the Omani capture is 12 December 1698 (Mombasa page's rulers list) or 13 December 1698 (siege page); the Ottoman interlude is 1585 (text) or 1586-1589 (infobox); Fort Jesus 1593 (inferred on the Mombasa page) or 1593-1596 (Fort Jesus page); the Fort Jesus page says the fort changed hands nine times between 1631 and 1895 or 1875.

What the Portuguese held between 1589 and 1698 north of Cape Delgado is not on these pages beyond Mombasa, Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa Island (the Omani gains of 1698); the Portuguese position at Malindi (allied since 1497, per the Kilwa page), Pate and Faza (destroyed 1587) is not recorded. The Portuguese holdings of 1505-1513 at Kilwa (Fort Santiago) are in the kilwa-sultanate dossier as an occupation. A gap-filler should open the 'Portuguese conquest of Swahili coast' or Malindi pages for the 1589-1698 footprint. The first Portuguese takeover of Mombasa in 1505 and the 1528 destruction are on the Mombasa page without a lasting hold.

Counterparts: portuguese-empire (a dossier file exists; this colony should be listed in its successors/holdings), sultanate-of-oman (me-10), sultanate-of-mombasa (this batch, Mazrui era only), the Swahili sultanate of Mombasa 1502-1589 (no dossier).

Reviewer af-05 (2026-10-19): the Omani counterpart of 1696-1729 is now yarubid-dynasty (Cliopatria row 'Yarubid dynasty', 1626-1743, which draws the Tanzanian coast from 1700; the siege was led by Saif bin Sultan, and portuguese-empire's 1698 loss uses the same slug), not sultanate-of-oman, whose row starts in 1744.
